posts.title: Fat Over Lean
posts.description: One of the first things I do in the studio these mornings is touch a painting. Not with a brush. With the back of a knuckle, lightly, on a corner where it will not matter if I am wrong. It is a small, slightly absurd ritual, like a cook pressing the top of a loaf, and most mornings the answer is the same. Not yet. The surface gives a little. It holds the faintest print of my skin. Somewhere under the skin of the paint, the oil is still doing its slow work with the air, and there is nothing I can do to hurry it. So I put the kettle on instead, and relish my choice of first biscuit of the day. For years I have painted in acrylic, and acrylic taught me to be quick. You lay a colour down, you make a cup of tea, and by the time it is half sipped, the layer is ready to be painted over, scraped, glazed, or buried. The paint keeps pace with your impatience.
